10:
And to the entire congregation. They did not speak to Moshe alone at first because they did not want him to persuade them of their mistake, and Moshe was not concerned about what they would say because he saw the fruit they were carrying.
...
That they should be stoned to death. Their claims were refuted, and so they reverted to weapons of war like animals that cannot speak. Moshe tried to strengthen them with the words mentioned in Devorim. Here, however, he did not call out, “Who is to Hashem to me!” as he did after the Sin of the Golden Calf, because he was afraid of a civil war, or that they would all be lost, so he preferred not to take action.
